newsitem.title: FRANCE: France less optimistic on EU reform after Rome.
newsitem.headline: France less optimistic on EU reform after Rome.

text.p: French European Affairs Minister Michel Barnier said on Thursday he was less optimistic after a meeting in Rome on Monday that EU institutional reform could be completed in time to allow speedy expansion of the Union.
In a statement, a French parliamentary committee said Barnier expressed worry about whether the IGC could complete its work by a self-imposed deadline of the end of June.

"In the absence of an accord among heads of state and government, the inter-governmental conference could be prolonged beyond July 1 and, in that case, the process of enlargement would be delayed, since it cannot begin until six months after the closure of the IGC's work," the committee's statement quoted him as saying.
Barnier told the committee he believed many EU states were underestimating the importance of the reform process.
Barnier was reporting to the parliament about his meeting with EU ministers in the Italian capital during celebrations of the 40th anniversary of the EU's founding.
